newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SPORT-AUSTRALIA LEADS VS FRANCE IN DAVIS CUP-FEB 7.
newsitem.headline: SPORT-AUSTRALIA LEADS VS FRANCE IN DAVIS CUP-FEB 7.

text.p: Australia were on the verge of upsetting Davis Cup holders France after winning both of the opening singles matches on Friday to lead 2-0 before Saturday's doubles.

The Australians' lead came after Patrick Rafter staged a remarkable comeback from two-sets-to-love down to beat French number one Cedric Pioline 3-6 6-7 (5-7) 6-4 7-5 6-4 in the opening match of the tie on grass at Sydney's White City.

Doubles specialist Mark Woodforde then raced through his match to beat an out-of-sorts Arnaud Boetsch 6-4 6-4 6-3 in just 97 minutes to give Australia the chance to close out the tie in Saturday's doubles.
Woodforde will team up with long-time partner Todd Woodbridge in that match against the French pair of Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux.

The Australians will start as heavy favourites after Woodbridge and Woodforde, the world's best doubles pair, last month added the Australian Open crown to the Wimbledon, U.S. Open and Atlanta Olympics titles they won last year.
France, who beat Sweden 3-2 to win the Davis Cup last December, must win on Saturday to keep Sunday's reverse singles alive.
